citation: Lyu C, Zhou Q, Xiao X, Bai X, Pu Y, Zhu H, et al. Metagenomics next-generation sequencing of plasma combined with blood cells for improving the prognosis of early infection in patients with hematologic disorders: a real-world cohort study in northern China. Frontiers in Molecular Biosciences. 2026;13:1662559.
study_design: Retrospective single-centre real-world cohort (Department of Hematology, Tianjin First Central Hospital)

population.population_description: 231 patients with haematological disorders (leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, aplastic anemia, etc.) with suspected infection, all undergoing whole blood mNGS (plasma + blood cell fractions) and blood culture simultaneously. 208/231 (90.04%) classified as infected, 23 non-infected by final clinical diagnosis. HSCT 148/231 (64.07%); immunosuppressed 227/231 (98.27%).
population.haemato_subtypes: AML 112 (48.48%), ALL 42 (18.18%), mixed lineage leukemia 4 (1.73%), MDS 37 (16.02%), aplastic anemia 11 (4.76%), CLL 2 (0.87%), malignant lymphoma 11 (4.76%), multiple myeloma 4 (1.73%), others (ITP, anemia, hemophagocytic syndrome) 6 (2.60%).

neutropenic_status: Immunocompromised status defined to include neutropenia (including aplastic anemia) or current chemotherapy; no ANC threshold or neutropenia counts reported

specimens.type: whole blood 5 mL (plasma cfDNA + blood-cell fraction, mNGS)

index_test.platform_or_panel: Whole blood mNGS: PathoXtract mcfDNA (plasma) + HemoCyte pathogen-enrichment (saponin lysis, bead beating) extraction kits (Willingmed); KAPA Hyper Prep / Illumina DNA Prep libraries; 75-bp single-end NextSeq 550Dx, >=20 million reads; Kraken2 vs NCBI GenBank/RefSeq/nt; positivity RPTM thresholds: viruses >=3, bacteria/fungi >=8, cryptococcus/mycobacteria >=1

reference_standard: Final clinical diagnosis by two supervising clinicians (+ third adjudicator if disagreement) based on composite of all microbiological tests, radiology, and clinical findings; BSI per Chinese expert consensus, LRTI per Woodhead guidelines. mNGS findings classified definite/probable/possible vs unlikely per Karius-style criteria.

diagnostic_yield.basis: Whole blood mNGS positive rate 77.06% vs blood culture 21.65% (P<0.001), plasma mNGS 72.29% (P=0.285), CMT 82.68%. Reported vs final clinical diagnosis: whole blood mNGS sensitivity 81.73%, specificity 86.96%, PPV 98.27%, NPV 34.43%; plasma mNGS 76.44%/86.96%; CMT 45.19%/100%; BC 23.56%/100%.

additional_yield_vs_conventional: Whole blood mNGS identified 101 of 107 clinically relevant species (94.4%); plasma mNGS 88 (82.2%); 13 clinically relevant microorganisms (12.1%; 10 bacteria, 3 fungi incl. Rhizomucor pusillus, Aspergillus ruber) detected exclusively in the blood-cell fraction. Only 1% (2/231) positive by BC alone; pathogen-level agreement with BC 75% among co-positives and 55.26% with CMT.
turnaround_time: 15-20 h from sample receipt to report, median 17.5 h
therapy_change: Whole blood mNGS positively influenced treatment in 72.73% of patients (initialization 47, escalation 47, de-escalation 19, confirmed empiric therapy 55); no impact 61; negative 2 (0.87%). In BSI patients positive impact 83.74%; pulmonary infections 75.15%; 77.88% of infected patients benefited.
mortality_or_outcomes: In-hospital mortality 44/231 (19.05%); infected group 21.15% vs non-infected 0.00% (P=0.010); median hospital stay 26 days (IQR 14-37.5).

quality_flags.blinding_of_index_result: unclear (composite final diagnosis included all microbiological tests, i.e. mNGS itself)
quality_flags.overlap_risk: Final clinical diagnosis incorporates mNGS results (composite includes 'all microbiological tests') -> incorporation bias inflating sensitivity/PPV. Reported accuracy metrics are internally inconsistent: sensitivity 81.73% (170/208) with PPV 98.27% implies FP=3, but the reported positive rate 77.06% (178/231) implies FP=8; NPV 34.43% is inconsistent with specificity 86.96% given n=231. Full 2x2 therefore not reliably reconstructible.

quadas2_notes: Large all-haemato cohort with HSCT majority. No verbatim 2x2 table in main text (Figure 2B contingency tables are in image); the extracted accuracy metrics are arithmetically inconsistent (see overlap_risk), so no 2x2 recorded. Retrospective, single-centre; all patients received empiric antibiotics before mNGS. Index test well described (kits, thresholds). Whole-blood (plasma+cell) approach is novel; blood-cell fraction added 13 pathogens.

evidence_quotes.quote: We retrospectively analyzed the results of whole blood mNGS testing from 231 blood samples of hematological disorders patients with suspected infections.
Between June 2022 and March 2024, a total of 302 individuals who underwent whole blood mNGS testing were screened, of whom 231 met the inclusion criteria were included in the final analysis.

Among the 231 enrolled patients, whole blood mNGS yielded a positive rate of 77.06%, which was significantly higher than that of blood culture (BC) (21.65%, P < 0.001), but no significantly different from plasma mNGS (72.29%, P = 0.285) or CMT (82.68%, P = 0.132)

Using the final clinical diagnosis as the reference standard, whole blood mNGS achieved the highest sensitivity, 81.73%, followed by plasma mNGS (76.44%), CMT (45.19%) and BC (23.56%). BC had the highest specificity, 100%, followed by whole blood mNGS and plasma mNGS (both 86.96%). Whole blood mNGS also demonstrated a higher positive predictive value (PPV, 98.27%) and negative predictive value (NPV, 34.43%) compared with the other methods

Based on the final clinical assessment, 90.04% (208/231) of the patients were diagnosed with infection and were classified into the infection group, while the remaining 9.96% (23/231) were classified as the non-infected group.

The final clinical diagnosis of infection was evaluated by two supervising clinicians based on the composite reference standard: combined results of all microbiological tests, radiological testing results, and a summary of the patient clinical examining results and symptoms.

A total of 107 clinically relevant microorganisms were identified across all patients by whole blood mNGS, BC and CMT (including BC), comprising 69 bacterial species (including 3 atypical pathogens), 24 fungal species, 12 viral species, and two parasitic species. Whole blood mNGS demonstrated superior detection capability, identifying 101 of the 107 total species (94.4%). When whole blood mNGS was partitioned into its plasma and cellular components, plasma mNGS detected 88 species (82.2%), while an additional 13 clinically relevant microorganisms (12.1%) were identified exclusively in the blood cell fraction
The turnaround time (from sample receipt to report generation) for mNGS testing ranged between 15 and 20 h, with a median of 17.5 h.
Whole blood mNGS demonstrated the highest proportion of positive influence (72.73%), surpassing plasma mNGS (68.40%), CMT (incorporating BC, 37.66%), and BC (18.61%).
The in-hospital mortality rate was 19.05% (44/231), with a median length of hospital stay of 26 days (IQR 14–37.5)

The majority had hematologic malignancies, primarily acute myeloid leukemia (AML, 48.48%, 112/231), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL, 18.18%, 42/231), and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS, 16.02%, 37/231). Overall, 64.07% (148/231) underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and 98.27% (227/231) were immunosuppressed.

viruses were considered positive when RPTM ≥3; bacteria and fungi required RPTM ≥8 for positivity determination. For specific pathogens with high clinical significance including cryptococcus and mycobacteria, a lower threshold of RPTM ≥1 was applied

exclusion_reason: No verbatim 2x2 in text (contingency tables only in figure image) and reported sensitivity/PPV/NPV/positive-rate values are mutually inconsistent, so a reliable TP/FP/FN/TN cannot be reconstructed; final clinical diagnosis also incorporates mNGS.
